name: Honda Activa 6G (DLX)
description: India's highest-selling petrol scooter. Extremely reliable, hassle-free maintenance, and omnipresent service network.
best_suited_for: Daily household commutes, quick errands, and riders who value effortless reliability and high resale liquidity.
pros: Unmatched brand reliability and massive service network
Instant refueling anywhere across India
Robust metal body construction and comfortable ergonomics
cons: Higher fuel running cost (~₹2.04/km at ₹102/L)
Basic analog/semi-digital console with minimal smart features
Regular oil and periodic engine maintenance required

name: TVS Jupiter 110
description: A refined family scooter offering plush suspension, external fuel lid convenience, and dependable fuel economy.
best_suited_for: Family riders seeking comfortable ride quality, generous legroom, and dependable city mileage.
pros: External fuel filler cap saves convenience at petrol bunks
Very comfortable plush telescopic suspension
Excellent value-for-money pricing in 110cc segment
cons: Petrol running expense accumulates over high monthly distances
Engine feels stressed above 75 km/h
Frequent servicing visits needed compared to EVs

name: Suzuki Access 125
description: The benchmark 125cc petrol scooter combining peppy acceleration, classic retro styling, and lightweight flickability.
best_suited_for: Urban professionals and college commuters wanting brisk throttle response with retro charm.
pros: Eager 125cc engine pickup with quick mid-range pull
Very lightweight chassis and easy center-stand operation
Spacious flat floorboard and large underseat bay
cons: Slightly lower fuel economy (48 kmpl) than 100-110cc peers
Running cost remains above ₹2.10/km
Service center coverage is smaller than Hero or Honda

name: Hero Splendor Plus XTEC
description: India's undisputed fuel economy king. Minimal upkeep costs, legendary durability, and cheap spare parts everywhere.
best_suited_for: High-distance commuters, delivery partners, and budget-conscious buyers seeking rock-bottom running and repair costs.
pros: Outstanding 65 km/l real-world petrol mileage
Lowest spare parts pricing and universal mechanics anywhere in India
Near 600+ km range on a single full tank of 9.8 litres
cons: Barebones styling and modest power output (8 bhp)
Skinny tyres and basic drum braking dynamics
Still consumes petrol and emits exhaust CO2 emissions

name: Honda Shine 125
description: The gold standard of smooth 125cc commuter motorcycles with a 5-speed gearbox and quiet eSP technology.
best_suited_for: Riders commuting 40-70 km daily who want a quiet, vibration-free ride with highway overtaking capability.
pros: Buttery-smooth engine refinement and quiet silent-start
5-speed gearbox enables relaxed 70-80 km/h cruising
Very high market resale value
cons: Running costs (~₹1.85/km) remain substantially higher than electric bikes
Traditional styling lacks youth appeal
Periodic chain lubing and engine oil upkeep

name: Bajaj Pulsar 150 Twin Disc
description: An iconic Indian sporty commuter bike known for muscular road presence, DTS-i punch, and highway stability.
best_suited_for: Young riders and weekend commuters wanting sporty acceleration, road presence, and highway touring freedom.
pros: Strong 14 PS engine with great top-end pull and disc brake confidence
Huge 15-litre tank gives ~650 km cruising range without stopping
Immense emotional appeal and muscular wolf-eyed front styling
cons: Heaviest running cost in commuter class (~₹2.27/km)
Higher annual maintenance with sportier parts and disc pads
Heavy kerb weight (148 kg) can be tiring in tight bumper traffic

name: Royal Enfield Classic 350
description: Timeless retro cruiser motorcycle with the signature J-series engine thump, heavyweight road authority, and touring comfort.
best_suited_for: Long-distance tourers and lifestyle riders who prize acoustic presence and relaxed open-road touring over pure economy.
pros: Iconic retro charisma, unmatched road presence, and heavy cruising stability
Vibration-free J-series 349cc engine with strong low-end torque
Limitless highway freedom without charging anxiety
cons: High purchase price and running cost (~₹2.91/km)
Heavyweight (195 kg) not ideal for short congested city errands
Substantial annual maintenance and tire wear expenses

name: Ola S1 Pro (Gen 2)
description: High-performance electric scooter with class-leading top speed, 4 kWh battery, cruise control, and connected touchscreen tech.
best_suited_for: Daily commuters travelling 40-70 km with dedicated home/office charging who want top-tier acceleration and smart features.
pros: Blistering acceleration (0-40 in 2.6s) and 120 km/h top speed
Remarkable running cost savings (~₹0.22/km vs ₹2.00+ for petrol)
Standard 8-year battery warranty coverage
cons: Requires dedicated 15A home/office socket or public Hypercharger access
Software glitches and service turnaround can occasionally be inconsistent
Substantial upfront purchase premium over petrol scooters

name: Ola S1 X (3 kWh)
description: Affordable mass-market electric scooter bringing EV running economics directly to petrol 110cc scooter price points.
best_suited_for: Budget-focused city commuters with home charging who want an EV that matches petrol scooter pricing.
pros: Ex-showroom price under ₹90,000 rivaling petrol Activa/Jupiter
Very low electricity running expense (~₹0.22/km)
8-year battery warranty gives peace of mind
cons: Physical key and segment-basic segmented LCD screen (no touchscreen)
7.4 hours standard charge time for full top-up
Needs reliable 5A/15A socket at ground parking

name: Ather 450X (3.7 kWh)
description: The engineering benchmark among Indian electric scooters. Renowned for razor-sharp handling, true Google Maps, and Ather Grid fast charging.
best_suited_for: Discerning tech enthusiasts and urban professionals who demand premium build quality, predictable battery thermal management, and rapid fast-charging.
pros: Exceptional build engineering, balance, and sports-car like handling
Ather Grid fast charging network across 150+ Indian cities
Accurate Google Maps dashboard navigation and stable OTA updates
cons: High upfront pricing (₹1.5L+ on-road)
True range is ~110-115 km in smart eco mode, less in Warp mode
Smaller underseat storage compared to family scooters

name: Ather Rizta Z (3.7 kWh)
description: Ather's purpose-built family scooter featuring the longest seat in the category, 34L underseat storage, backrest, and SkidControl safety.
best_suited_for: Families, couples, and utility riders prioritizing seat comfort, massive boot space, and pillion back support.
pros: Longest seat in the Indian scooter industry with supportive backrest
Huge 34L underseat boot + optional frunk luggage solution
Traction control (SkidControl) for wet monsoons and gravel
cons: Top speed capped at 80 km/h (family-oriented tuning)
Substantial upfront cost over petrol Activa
Home parking plug required for daily overnight charging

name: TVS iQube (3.4 kWh)
description: A conventional, whisper-quiet electric scooter from legacy automaker TVS with reliable electrical architecture and comfort.
best_suited_for: Skeptical buyers transitioning from petrol who want a familiar, conservative scooter feel backed by TVS authorized dealerships.
pros: Traditional scooter ergonomics that make seniors and family members comfortable
Extremely smooth throttle calibration without jerky regenerative braking
Widespread TVS dealership and EV service presence
cons: Modest top speed of 78 km/h
Conservative 100 km real range requires charging every 2-3 days
Charger carrying takes up underseat space

name: Bajaj Chetak Premium
description: Full sheet-metal body electric scooter blending iconic Indian Chetak heritage with modern European aesthetics.
best_suited_for: Style-conscious urban riders who love full-metal craftsmanship, retro curved lines, and dependable city commute.
pros: Durable, seamless all-metal bodywork with premium paint finish
Built-in onboard charger for convenient plug-in at any standard 5A socket
Sequential LED indicators and elegant retro digital dial
cons: Top speed limited to 73 km/h
Heavy metal body slightly limits acceleration compared to Ola or Ather
Limited rear boot capacity

name: Revolt RV400
description: One of India's few mainstream electric street bikes featuring swappable battery capability and simulated motorcycle exhaust sounds.
best_suited_for: Motorcycle enthusiasts seeking zero fuel expenses, removable indoor battery charging, and upright street posture.
pros: Removable battery can be carried indoors to charge in high-rise apartments
Sporty motorcycle ergonomics with upside-down front forks
Customizable artificial engine acoustic exhaust speaker
cons: Range drops to ~80 km in Sport mode
Belt drive requires tension inspection and protection from road debris
Limited dealer presence in tier-2 and tier-3 towns
